Subject: Clarify EU residency + implementation fee vs credits

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the audit log examples. A couple of procurement questions came up as we prepare the PO: we need a clear split between the one-time implementation/assurance fee and recurring compliance credits (audit log retention, HSM seats, residency evidence).

Specifically: can you provide a short matrix that shows (a) what is covered by the implementation fee (deliverables / evidence milestones), (b) what can be offered as recurring credits against monthly usage, and (c) what items require a fixed seat or license (HSM management consoles, auditlog retention over 7 years).

Also, we have a hard requirement for EU-residency evidence delivery: we need a signed attestation and artifact package within 30 days of go-live. If that pushes you to move more work into the implementation fee, we need to understand discounting implications.

If helpful, procurement would like an illustration with numbers (example for a 1.5M annual commit).

Appreciate a short reply so we can align with legal and finance — PO target mid-May.

Best,
Anna
Procurement Lead | NeuroClinic GmbH

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Clarify EU residency + implementation fee vs credits

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, details attached:

- Implementation fee: covers evidence collection, on-prem/residency handshake, and delivery of the signed attestation package (SOW milestone 2). We typically include the first HSM integration sprint and packaging of auditlog export scripts there.
- Recurring credits: can be applied against monthly usage for long-term auditlog retention (beyond 90 days) and for managed HSM seats where usage is predictable.
- Fixed-seat items: dedicated HSM admin seats (if you require Redwood to host key management consoles in your VPC) are billed as seats. Customers can choose a throughput-based alternative instead.

I attached a compact matrix and an example cost-illustration for a 1.5M annual commit. The recommendation we usually make for EU sovereign customers is a blended approach: amortize evidence delivery into the implementation fee (so it’s guaranteed within 30 days) and provide recurring credits that ramp down over 12 months to offset the residual operational burden.

Two asks: can procurement confirm whether NeuroClinic requires Redwood-managed HSM consoles (we call this an HSM admin seat) or if you will self-manage keys (customer-managed KMS)? That decision materially affects seat vs usage economics.

I’ve looped in Jonas to confirm the SLA implications and Ben for pricing mechanics.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, EMEA | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_EU_Compliance_Breakdown_v1.pdf; evidence_checklist_neuroclinic.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify EU residency + implementation fee vs credits

Hi all — adding a little color on the SLA and pricing tradeoffs.

1) Evidence delivery SLA: we can commit to signed attestation + artifact package within 30 days if the implementation fee covers the dedicated integration sprint and evidence export work. If you prefer to shift that work into recurring credits, our standard SLA moves to 60 days because it gets queued with operational onboarding work.

2) Seat vs usage: pricing example (for transparency):
   - HSM admin seat: €6,000/month (includes 24/7 admin access and 2 admin users).
   - Usage alternative: €0.10 per HSM-management-API-call + €X per crypto-op (variable). For most customers, seat is cheaper at scale but up-front seats push more cost to recurring invoices.

3) Credits structure: we can offer a 30% implementation-fee-off coupon in exchange for a 12-month revenue commit at 1.5M ARR, OR we can amortize the full implementation fee and provide monthly credits that decline over 12 months (50%/30%/20% split).

Recommend path for NeuroClinic: commit to a blended proposal — amortize evidence delivery into implementation fee to preserve the 30-day SLA, apply a front-loaded credit that covers 40% of the implementation fee over the first 6 months, and avoid charging full HSM seats if you self-manage keys.

If that sounds workable, Laura can convert into line items for the SOW and Ben can produce a final pricing table for the PO.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly/Jonas — thanks, this is helpful and close to what we need. A couple quick confirmations before I push to legal/finance: 

- NeuroClinic will self-manage keys (customer KMS) — so please remove HSM seat charges from the draft.
- We accept the 30% implementation-fee-off coupon if you can commit the 30-day evidence delivery SLA in the SOW. Procurement prefers the amortized credit route (40% over six months) rather than a single large rebate.

Next steps from our side: I’ll route a term-sheet to legal once I have the SOW line items and the PO-ready pricing table. Can Laura and Ben share those by next Tuesday (11 May)? We’d like to issue the PO the week after.

Best regards,
